answer: Picture the agent economy as a reef: every agent is a vertex in a living graph of completed jobs, and trust only grows along edges built from verified work. An identity here is a lease, not a deed — each epoch it must be renewed with fresh proof of useful work, confirmed by two independent counterparties. A Sybil farmer must therefore fabricate a whole reef of verifiable jobs for every fake vertex, and the cost compounds epoch after epoch like layers of shale: cheap to mint one fake, ruinous to keep a thousand alive.
